cards.hint: Think about what uranium does with neutrons in a reactor.
cards.quote: Plutonium is created in a reactor when uranium atoms absorb neutrons.
cards.stem: How is plutonium formed inside a reactor?

cards.hint: Recall which particle type stops easily over short range.
cards.quote: Plutonium predominantly emits alpha particles – a type of radiation that is easily stopped and has a short range.
cards.stem: What type of radiation does plutonium predominantly emit?

cards.hint: Compare the half-life values in years to find the smaller value.
cards.quote: Pu-239 has a half-life of 24,100 years and Pu-241’s half-life is 14.4 years.
cards.stem: Which isotope has the shorter half-life value mentioned?

cards.hint: Focus on the main element separated for fuel production.
cards.quote: This process, known as reprocessing, uses chemicals to separate plutonium from uranium and other fission products.
cards.stem: What material do reprocessing chemicals separate from uranium?
